facts.material: not stated; assumed brass (copper alloy), the usual material for faucet seats, stems and similar parts

gri_path: Section XVI note 2(b): faucet parts that are not goods of their own heading and are suitable solely or principally for faucets go with heading 8481 (parts of taps, cocks, valves)
GRI 1: heading 8481 covers taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances and parts thereof
GRI 6: 8481.90 parts > of hand operated and check appliances (faucets are hand operated) > 8481.90.10.00 of copper

rejected_alternatives.reason: applies if the parts are of iron or steel rather than copper alloy
applies if the parts are of plastics or other materials
parts of non-hand-operated valves; faucets are hand operated

missing_facts: What are the faucet parts made of (brass/copper alloy, steel, plastic)?
Which parts are they (seats, stems, cartridges, handles)? Parts of general use such as screws or washers go to their own headings.
classification.rationale: Faucet parts are dedicated parts of hand-operated taps, so Section XVI note 2(b) places them in 8481.90 under the parts of hand operated and check appliances. Assuming the common brass construction, the line is 8481.90.10.00 (of copper). In-force ruling L88053 classified brass faucet seats of unspecified origin in 8481.90.1000; a different material would move the part to 8481.90.30 or 8481.90.50.
